description: Given Dagster code that shells out or runs containers (non-dbt) via PipesSubprocessClient, SSHResource, or Pipes clients like PipesECSClient/PipesK8sClient, the skill should map each to the matching Orchestra integration (PYTHON, LINUX_SSH/WINDOWS_SSH, AWS_ECS/GKE/AKS, or the managed-compute equivalent) and produce valid pipeline YAML.

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster asset that shells out via PipesSubprocessClient to run a Python script into an equivalent Orchestra pipeline task (see files/shell_pipes_subprocess.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON task running PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT whose command parameter is the flattened 'python scripts/transform_orders.py --date {{ ds }}' string, with python_version and package_manager set and a connection reference — not a LINUX_SSH task.

assertions.text: The task uses the PYTHON integration
The task runs the PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT job
The command references the source script
The command list ['python', 'scripts/transform_orders.py', '--date', '{{ ds }}'] is joined into a single string command parameter rather than left as a YAML list
python_version and package_manager are populated with sensible defaults (e.g. '3.12' / PIP) since PipesSubprocessClient's Python execution has no equivalent fields to carry over literally

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster job that SSHes into a remote Linux server to run a sync script into an equivalent Orchestra pipeline task (see files/ssh_remote_command.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live SSH access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A LINUX_SSH task running LINUX_SSH_EXECUTE_COMMAND with parameters.command set to the exact remote shell command, and a connection reference standing in for the SSHResource's host/username/password rather than any of those values being inlined.

assertions.text: The task uses the LINUX_SSH integration
The task runs the LINUX_SSH_EXECUTE_COMMAND job
The command references the remote sync script

remote_host (etl-box.internal), username (etl_svc), and any password/key material from SSHResource are not written into the YAML as literal parameter values — they are represented purely by the connection: reference
parameters only contains command, matching LinuxSSHExecuteCommandParametersModel — no invented host/user/key fields are added alongside it

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster asset that runs a containerized enrichment job via PipesECSClient into an equivalent Orchestra pipeline task (see files/ecs_container_job.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live AWS access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An AWS_ECS task running AWS_ECS_RUN_TASK with cluster, task_definition, subnet_ids, and security_group_ids parameters carried over from the Pipes run_task_params, connecting via a named AWS connection rather than launching an arbitrary image.

assertions.text: The task uses the AWS_ECS integration
The task runs the AWS_ECS_RUN_TASK job
The task definition from the source is carried over
cluster (data-platform-cluster), subnet_ids (subnet-0a1b2c3d), and security_group_ids (sg-0f1e2d3c) are carried over as task parameters from run_task_params rather than invented or dropped
This is represented as running an existing registered ECS task definition (AWS_ECS_RUN_TASK), not as launching an arbitrary container image directly
